Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial generation latency pattern - Pinegrove Labs incident notification

Hi Jordan —

Short note to let you know we observed a recurring pattern this morning where a subset (~3%) of calls to your hosted model (pinegrove-prod, region: us-west-1) returned partial token streams and elevated tail latency (p95 -> p99) for windows of ~30–90s. The engineering team traced this to a hot-path KV-cache eviction race under a specific request size distribution.

What we did immediately:
- Activated a short-lived bypass for prefix-KV caching for your traffic to prevent eviction thrashing.
- Reran the routing policy to route ~20% of your traffic to a sibling pool with warmed caches.
- Raised priority for your requests so retry amplification is avoided.

Current impact: degraded tail latency for a small percentage of requests; no data loss and no leaked customer data.

We posted a brief notice on our status page (link below) and are running a full timeline capture for a postmortem. We will follow up within 24 hours with a remediation summary and next steps.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/20260907-349
Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (ops extract), ops_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook excerpt)

Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing a short-term mitigation that avoids rollbacks to your pinned model version.

If you want a quick sync, I can be on a call in 20 minutes.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Short answers:
- No observed token corruption. Partial streams are truncated early (client saw cut stream) but model outputs that fully completed repeated in sibling pool. We did not detect semantic changes to outputs for successfully completed responses.
- There were a few customer retries from SDKs; we throttled retry flows and suppressed automatic client-side retries for a window to avoid amplification.

I attached the incident_timeline.csv and a short ops runbook excerpt. We are preparing a consolidated log bundle and will share a postmortem draft by EOD Wednesday (24h).

Planned next steps (internal):
- Marissa: lead on postmortem draft and timeline consolidation.

- Stephanie: coordinate status page expansion and external messaging cadence + PR approvals.

I'll loop you in on the postmortem draft and the follow-up customer readout.
